title: Anand at nightfall
hook: the six ceremony pauris close the day in joy

segments.voice: Yesterday, Chaupai at nightfall, and your line, shelter for the night. Did you say its first line before the lights went out? Today, what comes after the shelter, as Rehras nears its end. Day four hundred sixteen.
screen: `CHAUPAI AT NIGHTFALL — SHELTER FOR THE NIGHT.`

segments.voice: A long day. You walk in, drop your bag, and before you've even sat down, someone puts a plate in front of you. Hot dal, a roti folded on the side, maybe a little achaar. You didn't ask. It's just there. Nobody makes a speech about it. You just sit. Safe first, then fed. That's the order the evening prayer follows too. Yesterday, the shelter. Today, the plate. Today: Anand at nightfall.
screen: `A LONG DAY. A PLATE PUT DOWN.` → `YOU DIDN'T ASK. IT'S JUST THERE.` → `SAFE FIRST, THEN FED.`

segments.voice: After the Chaupai asks for shelter, Rehras turns to joy: the six pauris of the Anand, the first five and the fortieth. You know them now. Anand bhaiaa meree maae: joy has come, my mother. And at the very end, anad sunahu vaddabhaageeho: hear the bliss, you fortunate ones. Notice the order inside Rehras. First, protect me. Then, joy has come. Fear is spoken to before joy is sung. And the joy isn't a reward for a good day. It's just what the night is given. Then, after the Anand, Rehras closes with two short passages that also come at the very end of the Guru Granth Sahib. The first is called the Mundavani, often explained as the seal, and it has a dinner-table picture of its own. In paraphrase, by Guru Arjan: on this plate, three things have been placed: truth, contentment and contemplation. The nectar of the Name is set there too, the support of all. Whoever eats it, whoever enjoys it, is saved. The second is a slok, also by Guru Arjan, a short, grateful confession. In paraphrase: I didn't appreciate what You did for me; You made me worthy. I have no virtue; You took pity on me, and I met the True Guru, my friend. So the evening prayer ends at a table. Shelter, then joy, then a plate with truth, contentment and reflection on it, and a thank you for what you didn't earn. Joy at dusk.
screen: `AFTER SHELTER, THE SIX PAURIS OF JOY.` · `PROTECT ME, THEN JOY HAS COME.` · `MUNDAVANI: A PLATE OF TRUTH, CONTENTMENT.` · `SLOK: YOU MADE ME WORTHY.` · then, large: `JOY AT DUSK.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hum anand bhaiaa. Sit back, as if you've just come home and the plate is in front of you. Hum, or softly say, anand bhaiaa meree maae, satguroo mai paaiaa. Joy has come, my mother; I have found the True Guru. Hum it two or three times, as slowly as you like. Then picture the plate: truth, contentment, a moment of reflection. Take one thing from it for tonight. Rest there. The bell holds the time.
Anand at nightfall. In Rehras, after the Chaupai's plea for shelter, the six pauris of the Anand bring joy, and the Mundavani sets a plate of truth, contentment and contemplation.
Your line: joy at dusk. Tonight, at dinner, before the first bite, notice the plate, and hum anand bhaiaa once, even silently. Day four hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: In Rehras Sahib, the Benti Chaupai and its savaiya and dohra are followed by six pauris of the Anand, then the Mundavani and a slok by Guru Arjan, the passages that also close the Guru Granth Sahib.

myth: in Rehras the Anand comes before the Chaupai
the Chaupai's plea for shelter comes first; then the six pauris of joy.
the Mundavani comes at the very end of the Guru Granth Sahib
it and the slok after it, both by Guru Arjan, close the scripture before the Raagmala.
the Mundavani's plate holds truth, contentment and contemplation
and the nectar of the Name, the support of all.

fork.setup: Rehras has just asked for shelter as night comes. what does it do next?
options: sings joy: the six pauris of the Anand.
fork.reveal: after protect me comes joy has come, and then the Mundavani's plate of truth, contentment and contemplation.

original.note: Gurmukhi: thaal, a plate; the Mundavani says three things are placed on it: truth, contentment and contemplation.

trapdoor: what you thought: Anand at nightfall is just the Anand again.
what it means: in Rehras the Anand's joy follows the plea for shelter, and the prayer ends at a plate of truth, contentment and contemplation.
what a scholar hears: the Mundavani and the slok tera keeta jaato naahee come at the close of the Guru Granth Sahib, before the Raagmala, so every Rehras ends almost where the scripture itself ends.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer tells the listener what they feel.

Mundavani paraphrased: on this plate three things are placed, truth, contentment, contemplation; the nectar of the Name, the support of all; whoever eats and enjoys it is saved. Slok M5 (tera keeta jaato naahee) paraphrased: I didn't appreciate what You did; You made me worthy; I have no virtue; You took pity and I met the True Guru, my friend. Confirm.
Mundavani as 'seal' (mundaa, a seal or ring): a common explanation, phrased as 'often explained'. Confirm.
The Mundavani and slok as the last passages of the Guru Granth Sahib before the Raagmala (Ang 1429): confirm phrasing; the Raagmala follows and its status is discussed among Sikhs.
Outline has no separate day for the Mundavani; it is folded in here since it follows the Anand in Rehras.
